newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr crawls higher in well worn range.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr crawls higher in well worn range.

text.p: The Australian dollar crawled higher at a thin midsession, extending a grudging short covering bounce begun when US$0.7720 support survived selling pressure.

It was assisted in the manouevre by a modest pullback in the yen which was overdue a correction after surging almost 10 percent against both the U.S. and local dollars in under a fortnight. Dealers said the Ministry of Finance clearly thought the yen rise had gone far enough for the moment and was also talking down the prospects of a hike in Japanese interest rates.
But the market needed to be certain US$/yen had stabilised before it could devote time to deciding the A$'s future.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) the dollar had edged to US$0.7775/80 from an early US$0.7763/68 and US$0.7762/67 late here Thursday.
Support was put at US$0.7750 but US$0.7720 remained the key bulwark after it absorbed heavy punishment on Thursday, while dealers expected fresh offers atop US$0.7780.
The upside was also thick with chart resistance folowing more than a month of choppy trading with US$09.7805, US$0.7835 and US$0.7860 all worthy of respect.
On the crosses the currency bounced to 90.71/81 yen from 90.13/23 late Thursday, in line with the U.S. dollar which made it to 116.67/70 yen from 115.75/85 late in New York.
Recent market concerns about a possible rise in Japanese interest rates eased a touch when the Bank of Japan said the emphasis for monetary policy would remain to make the recovery firmer.

The outlook for U.S. monetary policy remained a major uncertainty for the U.S. dollar with the market completely split on whether the Federal Reserve would tighten at its meeting next Tuesday. If rates were not raised the dollar was likely to come under renewed pressure, and AUD/yen with it.
In trade weighted terms the local currency firmer to 59.2 from 59.1 late Thursday. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
